narrative: A 17-year-old swimmer who had dreamed of representing her country in international competitions fled Syria with her older sister in 2015. The two boarded a boat with 18 others heading for the island of Lesvos, only about ten kilometers from the Turkish coast. The boat was overcrowded, and partway across the engine stalled; stranded at sea with the wind blowing, the sisters took turns in the water, pushing and holding the boat to keep it from sinking, and swam for more than three hours before the engine restarted and they reached the coast. She struggled afterward to understand why they made it when so many others did not; every report of a group drowning at sea took her back to clinging to the boat's rope, desperately treading water. She eventually made it to Germany, where she was received warmly and continued swimming, later competing at the Rio Olympics as a member of the first-ever Refugee Olympic Team and becoming a UNHCR Goodwill Ambassador.
